nodes.name: Hydrogen bubble template assisted electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Co foam/TP was fabricated by the hydrogen bubble template assisted electrodeposition process (see the ESI† for preparative details). When the reduction current was carried out to the working electrode, flower-like microballoons comprising ultrathin Co nanosheets were electrodeposited on the Ti plate. Simultaneously, hydrogen bubbles were produced at the electrode surface. As time goes on, hydrogen bubbles act as templates to build a 3D porous foam structure to obtain the Co foam/TP. A series of Co foam/TP electrocatalysts was prepared by varying the electrodeposition time to study its effect on the morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: Main diffraction peaks at 41.68°, 44.76°, 47.56°, and 75.94° assigned to (100), (002), (101), and (110) facets of metallic Co in hexagonal-close-packed phase (JCPDS No. 05-0727). Other peaks characteristic of metallic Ti.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Co foam/TP (Fig. 1b) denotes the main diffraction peaks at 41.68°, 44.76°, 47.56°, and 75.94°, which can be assigned to the (100), (002), (101), and (110) facets of metallic Co in the hexagonal-close-packed phase (JCPDS No. 05-0727), respectively. Other diffraction peaks are characteristic of metallic Ti (JCPDS No. 05-0682).

nodes.characterization_summary: Low- and high-magnification SEM images show unique 3D porous foam structure of numerous stacked ultrathin nanosheets on the TP substrate surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low- and high-magnification scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Fig. 1c) of Co foam/TP show a unique 3D porous foam structure of numerous stacked ultrathin nanosheets on the surface of the TP substrate (Fig. S1†).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM and corresponding EDX elemental mapping images show Co element distribution matching the morphology of Co foam/TP. Weak O signal observed from inevitable surface oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM and corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping images (Fig. 1d) denote that the distribution of the Co element has the same outline as the morphology of Co foam/TP. A weak O signal can also be observed from the EDX results (Fig. S2†), which arises from the inevitable surface oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p region shows metallic state at 778.6 and 794.1 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum in the Co 2p region (Fig. 1e) demonstrates the existence of a metallic state at 778.6 and 794.1 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image proves fine architecture of nanosheet subunits.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of Co foam (Fig. 1f) further proves the fine architecture of nanosheet subunits.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fringe with lattice distance of 0.206 nm corresponds to (002) crystal plane of metallic Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fringe with a lattice distance of 0.206 nm conforms well to the (002) crystal plane of metallic Co, which is seen clearly from the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of Fig. 1g.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: Co foam/TP shows higher capacitive current densities than Co film/TP, indicating larger electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This significant difference in performance is attributed to the 3D porous foam structure of Co foam/TP, providing a large number of electrochemically active sites and fast electron-transfer pathways, which can be evidenced by its better electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl, Fig. 2e and S13†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co foam/TP exhibits smaller charge-transfer resistance (Rct) compared to Co film/TP.
